claims.text: At 1:30 AM, local fishermen, skilled in the ways of the sea, found him 1.5 miles off Ong Dia beach and brought him safely back.
This rescue reflected the enduring community spirit and sea expertise of Mui Ne's local fishing community.
In early 2026, a separate event unfolded on Nguyen Dinh Chieu road, showcasing the sometimes volatile intersection of local and international cultures.

The incident sparked a dramatic 70-kilometer motorized police pursuit, putting the town in the international spotlight and highlighting the challenges that can arise in a bustling tourist destination.
Today, the Vietnam Kiteboarding School not only teaches the sport but also serves as a symbol of resilience and community.
Look towards the horizon, where Surfpoint Kiteboarding School stands as a testament to the evolution of sport and culture in this vibrant coastal town.
Surfpoint Kiteboarding School was co-founded in 2009 by Phong, a local who began his journey as a beach boy in 2003, and Peter, a European physical education instructor.
By 2006 and 2007, he had swept the 'King of Mui Ne' competitions, cementing his status in the kitesurfing community.
claims.evidence: Phong started as a beach boy in 2003, taught himself to ride, became an instructor, and by 2006 and 2007, he famously swept the 'King of Mui Ne' competitions.

claims.text: The main beach strip of Mui Ne is more than just a playground for kitesurfers; it is a cultural melting pot.
Schools here cater to diverse linguistic groups, with some focusing exclusively on Russian-speaking tourists.
claims.evidence: Mui Ne's main beach strip involves a cultural and linguistic divide between kite schools, with some schools catering exclusively to Russian-speaking tourists.

claims.text: The nearby Cham ruins stand as silent witnesses to centuries past, reminding visitors of the historical depth beneath the sands.
As you stand on the wind-beaten sands of Mui Ne, envision over a hundred kites dancing in the sky each December to February.
Here at the C2Sky Kite Center, distinguished by its strictly certified International Kiteboarding Organization (IKO) status, there's more at stake in the swift tailwinds than leisure.
claims.evidence: C2Sky Kite Center has historically operated as one of the few strictly certified International Kiteboarding Organization (IKO) schools on Mui Ne beach.

claims.text: Unlike the Surfpoint Kiteboarding School you visited earlier, this center focuses on safety.
